title: The rwb-comms operations and field names behind RWB-P6-E1055-CON
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 17; FSD P5 Document hub v3; TSD P5 Document hub v2
section: Story; Preconditions; Flow; Contract 12.1 and 12.2
description: RWB-P6-E1055-CON is the only contract this slice consumes, and no source names its operations, paths or request and response field names for the notice read and the dispatch reference, including the field by which the notice answer carries the document reference the INT-14 dispatch file uses.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-055 section 2 and section 4 step 2 name 'document reference' in the INT-14 file and DF-LEG-017 names notice.document_id; no extract gives the target operation name or its field list.
proposed: RWB-P6-E1055-CON publishes the notice read by notice ID and the dispatch reference as one operation with named fields, so rwb-document builds against a shape rather than a guess.

title: The document type of the WIN proof-of-delivery receipt and the notice-type to document-type mapping
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.3 and AC-ALT-P5-003-01; TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 document_type
section: Story; Flow; Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2; Data; Solution plan
description: The type table in force holds six types and none of them is a proof-of-delivery receipt, and the mapping from notice type DEMAND to document type DEMAND_LETTER is unstated. Both values decide the retention class and the write-once flag carried on the receipt row.
evidence: FSD P5 AC-ALT-P5-003-01 lists DEMAND_LETTER, COURT_NOTICE, APPRAISAL_REPORT, TITLE_DEED, SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT and GUARANTOR_NOTICE only; legacy RWB-E1-055 names no document type at all.
proposed: Add the receipt type to the type table, or confirm which of the six types a receipt is stored as, with its retention class and write-once flag, and confirm the DEMAND to DEMAND_LETTER mapping, at the next type table version.

title: The field names of the WIN receipt in document_field and the receipt granularity
source: TSD P5 Document hub v2 T3.1 document_field; FSD P5 Document hub v3 A2.9
section: Flow; Acceptance criteria AC2; Data; Solution plan
description: document_field.field_name carries no list of values, and no source names the field names used for the receipt facts (barcode, callback date, delivery status, sent type) or whether a receipt is one document per file or one per notice, so the case index cannot be asserted character for character.
evidence: TSD P5 T3.1 document_field: field_name varchar(60) with no list; legacy RWB-E1-055 section 11 names notice columns, not document fields.
proposed: Name the four receipt fields in the field_definitions of the receipt type and state the receipt granularity in the FSD A2 section for the proof of delivery.

title: The text of MSG-P5-016
source: FSD P5 Document hub v3 AC-EXC-P5-004-01; API Specification v4 note on the upload operation
section: Validation and messages; exception path X3
description: The FSD P5 upload exception flow names MSG-P5-016 for a file that fails the malware scan and gives the meaning only; no source read carries the message text, so the story cannot quote it and does not invent one.
evidence: FSD P5 AC-EXC-P5-004-01 'the response is 422 with MSG-P5-016'; the API note reads '422 uses MSG-P5-016 (malware found)'; no message catalogue entry is present in the extracts.
proposed: Add the text of MSG-P5-016 to the message catalogue so the upload refusal shows a written message instead of a placeholder.

title: The agent's document-read tool contract is not defined in any source
source: RWB-P10-E1062-CON; TSD P5 appendix T-A.2; Architecture v5 slide 16
section: Preconditions; Acceptance criteria AC1; Contract 12.1 and 12.2
description: No source fixes the name, the request fields or the response fields of the tool call the screening agent makes to read documents, and none says whether the agent reads one operation per document or one operation per case. Architecture v5 slide 16 states only the tag 'Document: tool: read extracted fields', and TSD P5 T-A.2 defines the P5 operations without an agent shape.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 16: 'REST Source data: tool: read case facts - Document: tool: read extracted fields'. TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-002, API-P5-003 and API-P5-009 give query and response names only for the P5 contract. Legacy RWB-E1-062 section 12 names P5 DocumentQueryService.listByCase and getFields in prose with no shape.
proposed: State in RWB-P10-E1062-CON that the agent's case read maps to API-P5-002 and its document read to API-P5-003, with API-P5-009 available for an extracted-field filter, and publish the tool call field names in the AsyncAPI and OpenAPI documents of rwb-document.

title: The idempotency-key format of DocumentStored and the event field names the agent reads are not defined
source: RWB-P10-E1062-CON; FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.19; Architecture v5 slide 42
section: Acceptance criteria AC2 to AC4; Contract 12.2 and 12.3
description: The FSD fixes in prose that DocumentStored is written to the outbox with the document ID, the case ID, the type and the source, and the event catalogue fixes the producer, the topic and the consumer, but no source gives the payload field names or the idempotency-key format the agent's contract expects for its run key SCREENING:<caseId>:<eventId>.
evidence: FSD P5 A2.2 AC-P5-002-01: 'DocumentStored is written to the outbox with the document ID, the case ID, the type and the source'. Architecture v5 slide 42 event 16 gives producer, topic and consumers only; its note says events carry IDs and facts, never personal data.
proposed: Fix the payload as documentId, caseId, documentType, source and storedAt, and state that the idempotency key is the outbox event ID, in the AsyncAPI document of rwb.document.events.v1 and in RWB-P10-E1062-CON.

title: The mask format and the per-role list of personal fields for SY-AGENT are not defined
source: TSD P5 T6.2; FSD P5 A2.6; Architecture v5 slide 41
section: Preconditions; Acceptance criteria AC1; Solution plan; Screens; Guardrails
description: The sources say that masking applies to personal fields and that rwb-access owns the masking policy, but none gives the mask format, the policy version label for SY-AGENT or the list of document fields the policy marks personal, so the masked read of AC1 and the field-level masking of the composite route cannot be fixed from a source.
evidence: TSD P5 T6.2: 'masking applies to personal fields'. FSD P5 A2.6 AC-ALT-P5-006-01: 'RW-CASEOWN, whose masking rule hides party names'. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-access 'scope, masking policy' with no field list or format.
proposed: Publish the mask format and the per-role field list with the masking contract of rwb-access, and state that SY-AGENT holds Documents R with every personal field masked and no clear value in the answer, the log or the trace.

title: The read behaviour for a stored document whose type has left the version in force is not defined
source: FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.19; TSD P5 T3.1
section: Acceptance criteria AC6; Solution plan
description: The FSD fixes the refusal of an unknown document type at store time with 422 and MSG-P5-006, and it fixes that a type row carries valid_from and valid_to, but no source says what a read returns for a document already stored whose type is no longer in the version in force.
evidence: FSD P5 A2.1 AC-EXC-P5-001-01 and A2.2 AC-EXC-P5-002-01: type BANK_STATEMENT refused with 422 and MSG-P5-006 at store time. TSD P5 T3.1 document_type: table_version, valid_from, valid_to, with no read rule.
proposed: State that a stored document is served with the type on its row and is never re-typed on read, and that the unknown-type refusal with 422 and MSG-P5-006 applies at store time only.

title: The number of synthetic documents per case and the version depth of a seeded document are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 4, 7 and 11; FSD P5 A2.3, A2.7 and A2.20; TSD P5 T3.1 and T3.2
section: Preconditions; Acceptance criteria AC2 and AC5; Solution plan
description: The legacy story fixes the case volumes and states only that case RW-2026-000001 has its documents linked; no source fixes how many documents a synthetic case carries, whether a case carries more than one document of the same type, or how many versions a seeded document carries. FSD P5 AC-P5-007-01 gives 180 sample documents, 30 of each of the six types, but that is the OCR sample of RWB-E1-049, shared across cases, not the case estate this slice seeds.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 AC1 reads 'Then case "RW-2026-000001" has its accounts, parties, interactions and documents linked' with no count; its section 11 gives 'DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-033 | document | all fields | Write' with no volume; FSD P5 AC-P5-007-01 reads 'the 180 synthetic sample documents, 30 of each of the six agreed types' as an evaluation sample; TSD P5 T3.1 gives document.doc_version and DF-DOC-025 previous_version_id with no count and no version depth.
proposed: Publish the per-case document count and the version depth with RWB-P1-E1065-CON in the Service Contract Catalog, and keep both as seed parameters of this story and of RWB-P5-E1025-APP so a change is a parameter and not a code release.

title: The file-name pattern of the synthetic documents is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 4 and 13; FSD P5 A2.1, A2.2 and A2.7; TSD P5 T3.1 document.storage_ref and document_intake.file_name
section: Preconditions; Acceptance criteria AC2; Solution plan
description: Every seeded document must have a file whose name the estate seeder writes into Blob and whose hash it records, but no source states the naming convention of the synthetic PDFs. The FSD examples name one runtime file per acceptance criterion, which are upload examples and not a generator pattern; TSD P5 gives the length of storage_ref and file_name but no format. Without a pattern the hash of a seeded document is not comparable across rebuilds and AC5 cannot be met.
evidence: FSD P5 AC-P5-001-01 reads 'a scanned court notice "notice-0001.pdf" of 1.2 MB'; A2.4 AC-P5-004-01 reads '"court-notice-0007.pdf" of 2 MB'; TSD P5 T3.1 gives DF-DOC-006 storage_ref varchar(400) and DF-DOC-049 file_name varchar(255) with no pattern; legacy RWB-E1-065 section 13 gives properties for seed, volumes and shape count only.
proposed: Fix the synthetic file naming pattern in the Service Template Specification next to the sandbox file properties, and state that the content of a file is derived from the seed value, the case ID and the type so that the hash is stable.

title: The DEV Blob container names, the rwb-document login name and the DEV read-only role name are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4, 7 and 10; FSD P5 A2.1; TSD P5 T6.1 and T6.2; Architecture v5 slides 8, 16 and 20
section: Preconditions; Authority; Solution plan; Screens and states
description: The seed must write each synthetic document to a container and each row must point at it, must run under a per-service login, and must be readable by a DEV-only read-only role. No source names the DEV storage account or the DEV containers, the rwb-document login, or a read-only role for the new schema; the legacy role name rwb_sandbox_read was granted on the pre-split schema recovery. The gateway-bff composite route and its field-level masking, through which SCR-30 and SCR-31 read the estate in DEV, are also unstated.
evidence: FSD P5 AC-P5-001-01 reads 'the file is in container "rwb-docs-legal" at "rwb-docs-legal/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1"' and AC-ALT-P5-001-02 reads 'the file is in container "rwb-docs"'; TSD P5 T6.2 reads 'service identities for jobs and agents' with no login name; legacy RWB-E1-065 section 4 step 10 reads 'grants SELECT on schema recovery to role rwb_sandbox_read' for the pre-split schema; Architecture v5 slide 20 gives the composite route per owner service with no route specification.
proposed: Record the DEV storage account and container names, the rwb-document login and the DEV read-only role in the Service Template Specification and the Service Catalog, and publish the SCR-30 and SCR-31 composite route with RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

title: The count of held intake items per exception shape and the pages each held item carries are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 4, 7 and 8; FSD P5 A2.7, A2.8 and A2.13 to A2.15; TSD P5 T3.1 and T3.2
section: Preconditions; Acceptance criteria AC4; Solution plan
description: Legacy BR4 fixes 10 cases for each exception shape and the FSD describes one held item per acceptance criterion, but no source states how many held intake items the sandbox carries per shape, how many pages each item has, or which review reasons the DEV estate must show for the review queue to be demonstrable. The lists of TSD P5 T3.2 name the allowed reasons and statuses; the volume behind them is absent.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-065 BR4 reads 'exception shapes generated' for cases only, 10 cases each; FSD P5 A2.7 AC-EXC-P5-007-01 describes 'a mailroom scan of 2 pages with no case and page 1 at quality 0.30' as one example; TSD P5 T3.1 gives document_intake.page_count and document_text.page_no with no volume.
proposed: Fix the held item count per shape and the page count per item as seed parameters with RWB-P1-E1065-CON, and name the review reasons the DEV queue must show in the test data section of RWB-P5-E1049-APP.

title: The exact idempotency-key format of rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 is not stated for the target topic
source: Template and Rules v1 R9; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 42; legacy RWB-E1-067
section: Acceptance criteria AC4; Contract 12.3; Solution plan
description: The legacy outbox header carried an idempotency key whose example is EV-02-RW-2026-000301-20261201, but no source states how the target DocumentStored key on rwb.document.events.v1 is formed, nor which CloudEvents attribute carries it.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-067 AC3 uses key EV-02-RW-2026-000301-20261201; Architecture v5 slide 11 fixes the record key as caseId and the CloudEvents envelope but names no idempotency attribute; TSD P5 T5.3 lists the event without a header schema.
proposed: Derive the key from the document row and publish it in a CloudEvents extension attribute, read from configuration, so AC4 and R-UNI-40 hold without a source for the format.

title: The CloudEvents attribute names that carry the actor and the occurred time on rwb.document.events.v1 are not stated
source: Template and Rules v1 R9; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 42; legacy RWB-E1-067
section: Preconditions; Contract 12.3; Solution plan
description: The legacy event header held the event ID, the idempotency key, the schema version, the occurred time and the actor. Architecture v5 fixes the envelope as CloudEvents but does not name the extension attributes that carry the actor and the idempotency key on the document topic.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-067 precondition cites an event header of event ID, idempotency key, schema version, occurred time and actor; Architecture v5 slide 11 lists the standard attributes only and the registry rule, with no actor attribute.
proposed: Carry the actor in a CloudEvents extension attribute alongside the standard attributes, and assert the envelope in the relay contract test against the AsyncAPI fragment of section 12.3.

title: The retry limit applied to the JOB-11 outbox relay of rwb-document is not stated
source: Template and Rules v1 R9; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 44; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-UNI-36
section: Acceptance criteria AC3; Business rules BR5; Solution plan
description: The consumer-side retry limit of the legacy story is three, before the exception queue. No source states the retry limit of the producer-side relay that publishes a pending outbox row, which this story reads as a parameter.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-067 states three retries then the exception queue; R-UNI-36 states the retry queue moves to EXCEPTION_QUEUE when retries are exhausted; Architecture v5 slide 44 gives JOB-11 as every minute in every service with no limit.
proposed: Read the relay limit from the platform relay configuration as a parameter with no value fixed in code, and test the pending-to-published loop rather than the count.

title: The JSON Schema registry subject name and the AsyncAPI document location for rwb.document.events.v1 are not stated
source: Template and Rules v1 R9; Architecture v5 slide 11
section: Contract 12.3; Solution plan
description: Architecture v5 fixes a JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility and an AsyncAPI document per topic, but no source states the registry subject name of the DocumentStored type or where the AsyncAPI document of this service is published.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 states AsyncAPI per topic and a JSON Schema registry with BACKWARD compatibility; slide 20 states every service is built from the template with contract tests; neither names a subject or a document path.
proposed: Name the subject and the document location from the platform naming and registry convention, and hold them in configuration so no value is written in code.

title: The contract shape rwb-case and rwb-document share for the case timeline is not specified
source: RWB-P3-E2016-CON; TSD P5 appendix T-A.2 API-P5-002
section: Preconditions; Contract 12.1 and 12.2; Solution plan
description: No source names the operation rwb-document serves for the case timeline, the names of the date-window query parameters, or the request and response field names on either side of the call. TSD P5 T-A.2 gives API-P5-002 the query type, page and size with no date window, while RWB-P3-E2016-CON consumes the document metadata of a case in the date range.
evidence: TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-002: Request 'Query: type, page, size'; Response 'DocumentPage'. RWB-P3-E2016-CON 12.2: 'GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents | P5 rwb-document | The document metadata of a case in the date range'.
proposed: Serve the case-scoped read on API-P5-002 of base /api/recovery/document/v1 with the window carried as from and to, inclusive, and the items carrying at, type DOCUMENT, summary, by, reference and doc_version; fix the names at the RWB-P3-E2016-CON baseline review with rwb-case and build both sides against the fake until then.

title: Whether the version count of a document travels on the timeline item or only on the document detail
source: TSD P5 T3.1 DF-DOC-011; legacy RWB-E2-016 AC1
section: Acceptance criteria AC1 and AC2; Data; Contract 12.1; Solution plan
description: The legacy story requires a document item and its version history on the timeline, and TSD P5 holds doc_version on document, but no source says whether the document item carries the version count or whether the count is read from GET /documents/{documentId}. The item fields of RWB-P3-E2016-CON hold no version field.
evidence: TSD P5 T3.1 document: DF-DOC-011 doc_version integer, Required Yes. TSD P5 T-A.2 API-P5-003 response Document: metadata, versions and extracted fields. RWB-P3-E2016-CON TimelineItem: at, type, summary, by, reference, reasonCode, fromQueueCode, toQueueCode, ruleId.
proposed: Return doc_version on the document item so the timeline shows the count without a second call, and return the full history on API-P5-003 when the item is opened.

title: The summary wording of a document timeline item is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-016 section 13; RWB-P3-E2016-CON sections 11 and 13
section: Acceptance criteria AC1; Business rules BR6; Contract 12.1; Screens and states
description: Both the legacy story and the case contract require a summary built from codes, but neither gives the template a document item follows, and RWB-P3-E2016-CON defers the summary template per type to the baseline review.
evidence: RWB-P3-E2016-CON: 'the summary template per type are settled with the consumers at the baseline review; this story fixes no value and invents none'. Legacy RWB-E2-016 section 13: 'TimelineItemMapper ... with summaries built from codes'.
proposed: Use the English label of the document type followed by the version count, built from rows only, and settle the exact wording at the screen review with RWB-P3-E2016-CON.

title: Which table supplies the document type label a timeline item shows
source: TSD P5 T3.1 document_type DF-REF-219 to DF-REF-221; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-07
section: Preconditions; Exception paths; Data; Contract 12.1; Solution plan
description: The document type code and its English and Thai labels are rows of document_type in rwb_document, so the owner holds them; DP-07 sends reference data and lists through the reference-data contract of rwb-case. No source says which of the two supplies the label an item displays, nor which column a locale shows and which row a document typed against an older type table version shows.
evidence: TSD P5 T3.1 document_type: DF-REF-219 doc_type_code, DF-REF-220 label_en, DF-REF-221 label_th, DF-REF-229 table_version, DF-REF-230 valid_from, DF-REF-231 valid_to. R5.5 DP-07: 'Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case'.
owner_role: Data steward and data product owner
proposed: Display the label from document_type at the version in force, label_en by default and label_th by locale, and compare the list with LOV-DOC-TYPE through the reference-data contract of rwb-case rather than copying it; fall back to the type code when the row of that version is absent.
